title: Privi Speciality Chemicals Ltd - 530117 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Privi FY26 revenue rose 21.7% to INR2,582.9 crore and PAT 75% to INR327.5 crore, with a 25.76% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR725.70 crore (up 15.29% YoY), EBITDA INR184.41 crore (up 25.09%) at a 25.41% margin, and PAT INR95.66 crore versus INR63.57 crore a year earlier. For FY26, income grew 21.73% to INR2,582.92 crore, driven by about 6.5% volume growth, roughly 8% price increases and product mix. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target and 20%+ EBITDA margins, with the first capex phase due by 30 June 2026 taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA. The PRIGIV JV turned profitable for the first time in Q4, and the merger with PFSPL and PBPL awaits NCLT approval.

segments.name: Standalone aroma chemicals (core)
segments.commentary: Management said demand for core aroma chemicals is steady, with about 70% of revenue from exports, mostly under contracts. Realisations rose from about INR450/kg to about INR600/kg over five years, per management.

segments.name: PRIGIV JV (with Givaudan, 51:49)
segments.commentary: Turned profitable in Q4 FY26 for the first time. Revenue is expected at about INR130 crore in FY27 versus INR55 crore last year, with an additional INR50 crore capex. It manufactures high-end specialty chemicals exclusively for Givaudan.

segments.name: Downstream / new specialty molecules
segments.commentary: Silver Amber, Amber Silk, Privilege and Privitolide are in commissioning, with one already commissioned. Ethyl maltol, maltol and cyclopentanone projects target mechanical completion by June 2027, with revenue expected over the next 18 months. Furfural backward integration is about 2 years away, and the vertical is said to reach about INR1,000 crore revenue.

guidance_outlook: Targets 20%+ revenue growth for the coming year on a standalone basis; the 20% excludes merged entities until the scheme is effective.
Expects to sustain 20%+ EBITDA margins going forward; one answer referenced a 24% margin and another 25%.
Long-term target of about INR5,000 crore revenue and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA in 3 to 4 years, roughly 2x.
Post all three capex phases, standalone capacity is expected at about 72,000 MT, around mid-to-late 2028.
Expects the NCLT approval for the merger of PFSPL and PBPL into the parent during FY27, internally targeted for Q3 FY27.
Expects state incentives of about INR13 crore a year, based on 50% of the GST on in-state sales in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: First capex phase to complete by 30 June 2026, taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA, with a calibrated ramp-up over the coming quarters.
Phase 2 of the multi-specialty aroma chemicals project is progressing as planned.

The three new-molecule projects (ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone) are in detailed engineering with procurement started; the 12 to 15 month build targets mechanical completion by June 2027, followed by about one month of trials.
A biomass-to-value-added-products demonstration plant with capex of about INR70-75 crore is in basic and detailed engineering, expected in about 12 months.
Furfural backward integration is expected around FY28-29, after first establishing the finished goods and sourcing furfural from outside in the meantime.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil attributed it to the timing overlap of annual raw-material and finished-goods contracts, which fall into Q4 and Q1, and said the business should be judged on an annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance inclusive of the proposed merged entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said the 20% is standalone as it stands today; the merged entities will be consolidated once the scheme takes effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital days rise amid the current situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Babani said any increase would be no more than 3-5%, because price rises tend to lengthen customer payment times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 forex gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said forex gains of about INR14 crore were recorded in other income, as the company is a net exporter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net-capacity and commissioning timelines after all three phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said about 72,000 MT standalone after the first three phases, with completion around June to September 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Can standalone EBITDA margins of 27-28% be reached at the consolidated level?
qa_highlights.answer: Narayan Iyer said consolidated margins should improve now that PRIGIV has turned profitable, but gave no level.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin improve next year given crude-linked input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil said the company will assume gross margin stays at a similar level, and that any upside will come from internal efficiency gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the decline in other expenses and power costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Patil credited the ProMax residual steam and power-saving programme and better freight and logistics contract pricing, per Narayan Iyer.

risks_watch: Crude-linked and West Asia disruption could raise freight, fuel and raw-material costs. Management said shipping may be delayed by a week or two, but stock cover is in place.
Q4 gross margin dip, which management attributed to contract timing; watch whether it reverses in Q1 FY27.
Execution risk on the 54,000 MT capacity ramp-up after 30 June 2026 and on the 2028 target of about 72,000 MT.
The NCLT approval timing for the merger (internally targeted for Q3 FY27) and its effect on consolidated numbers.
Demand for the new molecules at lower price points (for example about $45/kg); management is still testing market elasticity.
Biotech demonstration plant economics and capex, which management called complex and still at engineering stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term 5k story and margin sustainability, but cautious on biotech economics and on new-molecule pricing. Management deflected several questions on customer names and pipeline partners, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We have delivered 25% plus margins consistently across all quarters and for the FY 26 on the EBITDA numbers.
So we are covered for almost a quarter for regular raw material, which are contracted.
We are definitely likely to get there, because as I said, one of the key parameters there is what kind of products you are making.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR63.57 crore in Q4 FY25

demand_pricing: Management said demand for fragrance and flavour ingredients keeps growing, and that customers want reliable, compliant, non-China suppliers.
FY26 growth split: about 6.5% from volume, about 8% from price, and the balance from product mix.
Management said it expects to pass on raw-material-driven price increases, citing customer trust and a 1-2% price premium for supplier reliability.

Raw-material cover: renewable inputs under annual contracts have about 1 to 1.5 months of inventory plus about 1 month in transit. Other inputs have about 3 months in stock and 2 to 3 months in pipeline.
Management said about 70% of raw materials are imported, which partly offsets rupee-driven realisation gains.
Management said it is in discussions with other MNC partners but is too early to disclose.

adds.what: First capex phase taking installed capacity to 54,000 MTPA (calibrated ramp-up)
Three new-molecule projects (ethyl maltol, maltol, cyclopentanone) targeting mechanical completion June 2027

growth.why: Management reiterates ~20% standalone revenue growth for FY27, backed by the first capex phase (54,000 MTPA, due by 30 June 2026), PRIGIV revenue rising to ~INR130 crore from INR55 crore, and price pass-through; the 20% excludes merged entities, and the new-molecule projects only reach mechanical completion around June 2027.
